subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Microorganisms decompose dead material faster when conditions are:
options: Warm, moist and with plenty of oxygen
questions.explain: Decomposers are most active in warm, moist, oxygen-rich conditions, which speed up the breakdown of dead matter.

questions.q: Plants compete with each other mainly for:
options: Light, water, space and mineral ions
questions.explain: Plants compete for light, water, space and mineral ions from the soil, which they need to grow.

questions.q: In a food chain, what does the direction of the arrows represent?
options: The flow of energy (and biomass) from one organism to the next
questions.explain: Arrows in a food chain show the transfer of energy and biomass from one organism to the next.

questions.q: In the carbon cycle, how is carbon dioxide removed from the atmosphere?
questions.explain: Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the air, using it to make glucose in plants.

questions.q: Deforestation can harm the environment by:
options: Reducing biodiversity and increasing atmospheric carbon dioxide
Removing carbon dioxide from the air
questions.explain: Deforestation reduces habitats and biodiversity, and means less CO2 is absorbed, contributing to global warming.

questions.q: In a predator–prey relationship, what usually happens to the predator population shortly after the prey population rises?
options: It stays exactly the same forever
It rises, as there is more food available
questions.explain: More prey means more food, so the predator population increases, slightly after the prey peak.

questions.q: High biodiversity in an ecosystem is beneficial because it:
options: Reduces the number of food chains
Makes ecosystems more stable and resilient
questions.explain: High biodiversity makes ecosystems more stable, as species are less dependent on any single one.

questions.q: In the water cycle, water returns to the atmosphere mainly through:
questions.explain: Water enters the atmosphere by evaporation from water bodies and transpiration from plants.

questions.q: Which processes release carbon dioxide back into the atmosphere?
questions.explain: Respiration, combustion (burning) and decomposition all return carbon dioxide to the atmosphere.

questions.q: In a stable community, the numbers of predators and prey:
options: Both rise together and never fall
Rise and fall in linked cycles, with the predator peak following the prey peak
questions.explain: Predator and prey numbers cycle: a rise in prey is followed by a rise in predators, which then reduces the prey again.

questions.q: Why do food chains rarely have more than four or five trophic levels?
options: There is not enough energy passed on to support more levels
There are not enough species on Earth
Animals refuse to eat each other
questions.explain: So little energy is passed up each level that there is not enough to support many more top consumers.

questions.q: Which apparatus is used to estimate the number of plants or slow-moving organisms in a sample area?
questions.explain: A quadrat is a square frame placed (often randomly) to count or estimate organisms in a known area.

questions.q: How is carbon passed from a plant to a herbivore in the carbon cycle?
options: When the animal eats the plant, taking in carbon compounds
By the plant respiring onto the animal
questions.explain: Carbon locked in plant compounds (e.g. glucose) passes to animals when they eat the plants (feeding).

questions.q: What is meant by interdependence in an ecosystem?
options: Species relying on each other for things like food, shelter and pollination
questions.explain: Interdependence means organisms rely on one another (and abiotic factors), so a change in one affects others.

questions.q: A transect is used in ecological sampling to:
options: Investigate how the distribution of organisms changes across an area
questions.explain: A transect (a line across the habitat) is used to study how species distribution changes, e.g. with distance.

questions.q: A student uses ten quadrats placed randomly in a field to estimate the number of daisies. Why are the quadrats placed randomly?
options: To count only the largest plants
To avoid bias and get a representative sample of the whole field
Because daisies only grow in lines
questions.explain: Random placement avoids bias, giving a fair, representative estimate that can be scaled up to the whole area.

questions.q: In a food chain, what happens to most of the energy at each trophic level so little passes to the next?
options: It is lost through respiration, movement, heat and waste
It is stored permanently in bones
questions.explain: Most energy is lost via respiration, movement, heat and undigested waste, so only about 10% passes to the next level.

questions.q: In a food chain, organisms that make their own food by photosynthesis are called:
questions.explain: Producers, usually green plants and algae, make their own food by photosynthesis and start most food chains.

questions.q: Increasing levels of which gases are linked to global warming?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide and methane are greenhouse gases whose rising levels are linked to global warming.

questions.q: Which of these is a biotic factor that could affect a population of rabbits?
questions.explain: The number of predators is a biotic (living) factor; temperature, light and moisture are abiotic factors.

questions.q: Pollution of a river with sewage can reduce biodiversity because it:
options: Has no effect on living organisms
Lowers oxygen levels as microorganisms multiply, killing aquatic animals
questions.explain: Sewage causes microorganisms to multiply and use up oxygen, so fish and other organisms die, reducing biodiversity.

questions.q: In the food chain grass → rabbit → fox, the rabbit is a:
questions.explain: The rabbit eats the producer (grass), so it is a primary consumer (herbivore).
